recipes.name: Sweet Potato Curry with Chickpeas
ingredients: 2 TL curry powder, 1 TL cumin, ½ TL chili flakes
steps: Start cooking the rice.
Heat oil, fry onion for 3–4 Min until translucent, add garlic for 1 Min.
Stir in spices and toast for 1 Min.
Add sweet potatoes and canned tomatoes, stir to combine.
Put the lid on and simmer for 12–15 Min until sweet potatoes are tender.
Stir in coconut milk and chickpeas, simmer for another 5 Min, then season to taste.
Serve over rice.
recipes.tips: Topping: A dollop of yogurt or buttermilk on top makes it taste fresher. Swap: Stir in frozen peas or spinach at the end.
recipes.feedback: Perfekt für Hühnchen und noch anderes gemüse - wäre voll geiles Curry mit Brokkoli gewesen

recipes.name: Pasta e Ceci
steps: Heat oil, sauté onion for 3–4 Min until translucent, add garlic and cook for 1 Min.
Stir in cumin, paprika, and chili flakes, toast for 1 Min.
Add canned tomatoes, stir, and let simmer for 5 Min.
Stir in chickpeas. Add approx. 400ml water (depending on desired consistency).
Add pasta directly into the sauce and cook over medium heat until al dente — stir occasionally and add more water as needed.
Season to taste and serve with cheese.
recipes.tips: A splash of lemon juice at the end makes it taste fresher. If you prefer it creamier, mash a spoonful of chickpeas and stir them in.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Apple Cake with Crumble (Shortcrust Pastry)
ingredients: Dough: 200g butter, cold, cut into cubes
steps: Rub the flour, sugar, salt, and cold butter cubes together with your fingertips until coarse crumbs form. Add the egg and press together briefly — do not knead. Shape into a ball, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill for 30 Min.
Peel, core, and slice the apples into pieces about 3 mm thin. Toss with sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
For the crumble: work the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and cold butter together with your fingers until coarse crumbs form. Set aside in the fridge.
Preheat the oven to 180°C top/bottom heat. Line a baking sheet (approx. 30x40 cm) with parchment paper.
Press the shortcrust pastry evenly onto the baking sheet — about 5 mm thick, pulling the edges up slightly.
Arrange the apple slices tightly in overlapping layers.
Scatter the crumble evenly on top.
Bake for 40–45 Min until the crumble is golden brown. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
recipes.tips: Topping: dust with powdered sugar 🛒 before serving, or serve with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream 🛒. Swap: lemon juice can be left out, it works fine without it. Alltags-Upgrade: mix 50g chopped almonds into the crumble for extra texture. Technik: the butter really must be cold (freeze it briefly if needed), and don't slice the apples too thin or they will turn mushy.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Apple Cake with Streusel (Yeast Dough)
steps: Gently warm the milk (approx. 35°C — not hot). Stir in the yeast and 1 TL sugar, leave for 5 Min until foamy.
Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast milk, softened butter, and egg. Knead for 8–10 Min until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 60 Min until doubled in size.
Peel, core, and slice the apples, then mix with sugar and cinnamon.
Work the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and cold butter together into rough crumbles for the streusel.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a baking sheet (30x40 cm) or line it with parchment paper.
Roll the yeast dough out onto the baking sheet, press up the edges, and let it rest for another 15 Min.
Spread the apples evenly over the dough and crumble the streusel on top.
Bake for 35–40 Min until golden brown. Allow to cool.
recipes.tips: Topping: serve warm with whipped cream 🛒 or vanilla custard. Swap: yeast dough instead of shortcrust makes it moister and fluffier. Alltags-Upgrade: let the dough rise in a slightly preheated (30°C) then switched-off oven — rises reliably every time. Technik: never heat the milk above 45°C or the yeast will die. Best enjoyed fresh or the next day.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Apple Cake with Crumble Topping (Baking Powder Batter)
ingredients: Dough: 1 Päckchen vanilla sugar 🛒 (or 1 TL cinnamon)
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C top/bottom heat. Grease and flour a baking sheet (30x40 cm) or line it with parchment paper.
Beat the softened butter with the sugar and vanilla sugar until creamy. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each.
Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt, then stir into the butter mixture alternately with the milk until smooth.
Spread the batter evenly over the prepared baking sheet.
Toss the apples with the sugar and cinnamon, then arrange them closely over the batter.
Mix the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and cold butter together to form a crumble and scatter it over the apples.
Bake for 40–45 Min until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
recipes.tips: Topping: Dust with powdered sugar 🛒 or add a dollop of whipped cream. Swap: Replace the vanilla sugar with 1 TL cinnamon — entirely from pantry staples. Alltags-Upgrade: the quickest version with no waiting time; adding 50g ground almonds to the crumble gives extra texture. Keeps for 3–4 days covered at room temperature.

recipes.name: Porridge with Apple & Cinnamon
ingredients: 300ml milk (or a mix of water and milk)
steps: Add the rolled oats, milk, and a pinch of salt to a saucepan.
Simmer, stirring, for 5–7 Min until creamy.
Stir in the diced apple and cinnamon, and let it warm through briefly.
Spoon into bowls and top with honey and almonds.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted almonds or sunflower seeds and a few banana slices. Swap: instead of apple, stir in mashed banana (then use less honey). Alltags-Upgrade: stir in 1 EL peanut butter for a creamier, more filling result.

recipes.name: Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie
steps: Add all ingredients to the blender.
Blend for 30–60 Sek until smooth and frothy.
Taste and add more milk if a thinner consistency is desired.
Serve immediately.
recipes.tips: Topping: a few oats and a sprinkle of cinnamon on top. Swap: leave out the honey if the bananas are very ripe. Alltags-Upgrade: use 1 frozen banana overnight — makes the smoothie ice-cold and creamy like a milkshake.

recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs with Cheese on Toast
steps: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat.
Pour in the eggs and slowly let them set using a spatula, stirring as you go.
Just before they are fully set, stir in the cheese and remove from the heat.
Serve on toasted bread and sprinkle with chives.
recipes.tips: Topping: Chives or chili flakes and a few slices of tomato. Swap: Leave out the cheese and season with paprika instead. Alltags-Upgrade: Toast the bread in the butter before adding the eggs — it adds extra flavor.

recipes.name: Shakshuka
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan and sauté the onion and bell pepper for 5 Min until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chili flakes and fry for 1 Min, stirring.
Add the canned tomatoes, season with salt and pepper and simmer for 10 Min until thick and saucy.
Use a spoon to press wells into the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–8 Min until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Sprinkle with feta and parsley and serve with bread.
recipes.tips: Topping: crumbled feta, parsley and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: skip the feta and add extra paprika to keep it entirely pantry-based. Alltags-Upgrade: stir in a can of chickpeas while simmering = more filling and a complete dinner.

recipes.name: Apple Pancakes
ingredients: honey 🛒 or powdered sugar 🛒 for serving
steps: Whisk together flour, milk, eggs, sugar, and salt into a smooth batter and let it rest for 10 Min.
Cut the apples into thin slices and mix with cinnamon.
Melt butter in a pan and lay in a few apple slices.
Pour a ladle of batter over the apples and cook over medium heat until golden brown, then flip.
Serve with honey or powdered sugar. Cook the remaining batter the same way.
recipes.tips: Topping: cinnamon sugar, honey, or a dollop of buttermilk. Swap: banana instead of apple in the batter. Alltags-Upgrade: add a handful of oats to the batter for a slightly heartier and more filling pancake. Technik: letting the batter rest ensures a lighter, more tender result.

recipes.name: French Toast (Arme Ritter)
steps: Whisk together eggs, milk, sugar, and cinnamon in a shallow bowl.
Briefly dip the bread slices in the egg mixture on both sides, letting them soak slightly.
Heat butter in a pan.
Fry the slices over medium heat until golden brown, then flip.
Serve with honey, cinnamon sugar, or banana slices.
recipes.tips: Topping: Cinnamon sugar and banana slices, or applesauce. Swap: skip the sugar in the batter and go savory with cheese — makes a great lunch instead. Alltags-Upgrade: perfect for day-old bread — rescues leftovers and actually tastes even better than with fresh bread.

recipes.name: Quick Vegetable Pan with Rice
steps: Cook the rice in a rice cooker or pot.
Heat oil in a large pan, fry the onion for 2 Min.
Add the zucchini, bell pepper, and frozen vegetables; fry on high heat for 6–8 Min.
Briefly fry the garlic and chili flakes with the vegetables.
Add the cooked rice, deglaze with soy sauce, and stir-fry everything for 2–3 Min.
Optionally, crack an egg at the edge of the pan, let it set, then stir it in.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted sunflower seeds and chili flakes. Swap: replace soy sauce with salt + paprika powder if you don't have any. Alltags-Upgrade: use day-old rice — fried rice turns out much better with cold rice (fluffy instead of mushy).

recipes.name: Quick Tuna Pasta
steps: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat oil, sauté onion until translucent, then add garlic and chili.
Stir in canned tomatoes, simmer for 8 Min, and season with salt and pepper.
Roughly stir in the tuna and let it warm through for 2 Min.
Drain the pasta and mix with the sauce.
Serve with Parmesan.
recipes.tips: Topping: Chili flakes and a squeeze of lemon. Swap: Chickpeas instead of tuna for a vegetarian version. Alltags-Upgrade: Stir 1 EL of the sauce with a little pasta water until smooth — this helps the sauce coat the pasta nicely.

recipes.name: Chickpea Couscous Bowl
steps: Pour an equal amount of boiling salted water over the couscous, cover, and let it steam for 5 Min, then fluff with a fork.
Toast the chickpeas in a pan with a little oil and cumin for 5 Min.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Mix everything together and season to taste with lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Top with parsley and feta.
recipes.tips: Topping: Feta, parsley, and a few roasted chickpeas on top. Swap: Bulgur instead of couscous (then let it steam for 12 Min). Alltags-Upgrade: Roast the chickpeas with paprika until crispy — adds bite and warmth to the bowl. Keeps well for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Bulgur Vegetable Skillet
steps: Heat oil, sauté onion until translucent, then add garlic.
Add bell pepper and zucchini, fry for 5 Min.
Briefly toast the paprika powder and cumin.
Stir in bulgur and canned tomatoes, add 400ml water.
Put the lid on, simmer for 12 Min until the bulgur is soft and the liquid is absorbed.
Season to taste and let rest briefly.
recipes.tips: Topping: a dollop of buttermilk and chili flakes. Swap: use frozen vegetables instead of fresh when you're short on time. Alltags-Upgrade: stir in chickpeas = more protein and a complete one-pot meal.

recipes.name: Quick Asian Stir-Fry Noodles
steps: Cook noodles according to package instructions, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan over high heat, stir-fry the bell pepper and frozen vegetables for 4–5 Min.
Add the garlic and ginger and fry briefly.
Push the vegetables to the side, crack the eggs into the center and let them set, then stir everything together.
Add the noodles and soy sauce, stir-fry everything for 2–3 Min.
Season to taste with chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: soy sauce, chili flakes, and toasted sunflower seeds as a sesame substitute. Swap: leave out the egg and use chickpeas or tuna instead. Alltags-Upgrade: a splash of honey in the soy sauce gives you that classic sweet-salty wok flavor.

recipes.name: Red Bean Skillet with Eggs
steps: Heat oil and fry onion and bell pepper for 5 Min.
Toast the cumin, paprika, and chili briefly.
Add canned tomatoes and beans, simmer for 5 Min, season to taste.
Use a spoon to make wells, then crack the eggs into them.
Scatter cheese on top, put the lid on, and cook for 6–8 Min until the eggs are set.
Serve with bread or rice.
recipes.tips: Topping: grated cheese, chili flakes, a dollop of buttermilk as a sour cream substitute. Swap: chickpeas instead of red beans. Alltags-Upgrade: leftovers the next day eaten cold with bread or in a wrap — the flavors meld together and it tastes even better. Technik: keep the heat low once the eggs go in so the whites set gently without the bottoms burning.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
steps: Cook the spaghetti al dente in plenty of salted water, reserving some pasta water.
Warm the olive oil over medium heat and slowly fry the garlic and chili flakes until golden (not brown).
Remove the pan from the heat and add a ladleful of pasta water.
Add the spaghetti and toss to coat with the garlic-oil emulsion.
Season with salt, pepper, and parsley, and add Parmesan to taste.
recipes.tips: Topping: plenty of freshly ground pepper and a touch of Parmesan. Swap: skip the parsley and use a little grated lemon zest for freshness instead. Alltags-Upgrade: the starchy pasta water is the secret — it makes the oil creamy and stops it from separating. Never let the garlic burn or it will turn bitter.

recipes.name: Pasta with Tomato Cream Sauce & Vegetables
steps: Cook pasta al dente.
Heat oil, sauté onion until translucent, then cook zucchini for 5 Min.
Briefly fry garlic and paprika.
Add canned tomatoes and simmer for 5 Min.
Stir in cream, season to taste, and let rest for 2 Min.
Mix in pasta and serve with cheese.
recipes.tips: Topping: grated cheese and chili flakes. Swap: bell pepper or frozen vegetables instead of zucchini. Alltags-Upgrade: fry a spoonful of tomato paste along with the garlic for a deeper, rounder tomato flavor.

recipes.name: One-Pot Pasta with Spinach
steps: Heat oil in a large pot, sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Add pasta, frozen spinach, and approx. 700ml water; season with salt.
Bring to a boil and simmer, stirring occasionally, for approx. 10–12 Min until the pasta is cooked and the water is almost fully absorbed.
Stir in cream and nutmeg, then season to taste.
Serve sprinkled with cheese.
recipes.tips: Topping: nutmeg, pepper, and grated cheese. Swap: fresh spinach (stir in at the end) or frozen peas. Alltags-Upgrade: everything in one pot — no draining pasta water, less washing up, and the pasta absorbs the sauce directly.

recipes.name: Baked Feta Pasta
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place the tomatoes and whole garlic cloves in a baking dish and set the block of feta in the center.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with chili, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 25–30 Min until the tomatoes burst and the feta is soft.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta al dente.
Squeeze out the garlic, stir everything in the dish into a creamy sauce, mix in the pasta, and serve with basil.
recipes.tips: Topping: fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: regular tomatoes cut into wedges instead of cherry tomatoes. Alltags-Upgrade: practically runs itself in the oven — the roasted tomatoes and feta come together into a creamy sauce with no extra effort. Leftovers taste great cold as a pasta salad.

recipes.name: Vegetable Lasagne
steps: Heat oil, fry onion, zucchini and bell pepper for 8 Min, then add garlic and paprika powder.
Stir in canned tomatoes, simmer for 10 Min, season with salt.
Béchamel: melt butter, stir in flour, gradually pour in milk, stir until smooth, season with nutmeg.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
In a baking dish, layer the tomato vegetables, sheets and béchamel alternately, finishing with béchamel and cheese.
Bake for 30–40 Min until golden brown. Leave to rest for 5 Min.
recipes.tips: Topping: add extra cheese and chili flakes in the last 10 Min. Swap: add frozen spinach to the vegetable layer. Alltags-Upgrade: prepare the day before and refrigerate — just bake the next day; the lasagne will also cut more cleanly. Technik: press the lasagne sheets gently into each layer so they absorb the sauce evenly.

recipes.name: Baked Pasta al Forno
steps: Cook pasta until only half done (it will continue cooking in the oven), then drain.
Heat oil, fry onion and zucchini, add garlic and paprika.
Stir in canned tomatoes and cream, season to taste.
Mix pasta with the sauce and transfer to a baking dish.
Top with cheese and bake at 200°C for 20–25 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: crispy cheese edges and chili flakes. Swap: add chickpeas or tuna to the sauce for extra substance. Alltags-Upgrade: works great with leftover pasta — just mix with sauce and cheese, put it in the dish, and pop it in the oven. Freezes well in individual portions.

recipes.name: Fried Rice with Egg
ingredients: 250g rice (best if from the day before)
steps: Cook the rice and let it cool completely (or use leftover rice from the day before).
Heat oil in a pan over high heat, then fry the onion and garlic.
Add the peas & carrots and fry for 3 Min.
Push the vegetables to the side, crack in the eggs, let them set, then break them up.
Add the rice, deglaze with soy sauce, and stir-fry everything over high heat for 3–4 Min.
Season to taste with pepper and chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: Chili flakes and a substitute for spring onions: thin raw onion rings. Swap: Frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas & carrots. Alltags-Upgrade: cold leftover rice from the day before is the key — it turns out grainy instead of mushy. Perfect for using up leftovers.

recipes.name: Couscous Salad
steps: Pour boiling salted water over the couscous in equal amounts, cover, let swell for 5 Min, then fluff with a fork.
Finely dice the vegetables.
Mix the couscous with the vegetables.
Stir together a dressing from lemon juice, olive oil, salt, pepper, and cumin, then fold it in.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve cold.
recipes.tips: Topping: Feta, toasted almonds, or sunflower seeds. Swap: Bulgur instead of couscous. Alltags-Upgrade: Add canned chickpeas and it transforms from a side dish into a hearty main course. Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

recipes.name: Bulgur Pilaf with Peas & Carrots
steps: Heat butter or oil and sauté the onion until translucent.
Briefly toast the bulgur until fragrant.
Add the paprika, canned tomatoes, and 400ml water, then season with salt.
Stir in the peas and carrots.
Put the lid on and simmer for 12–15 Min until the bulgur is tender.
Remove from the heat, let rest for 5 Min, then fluff up.
recipes.tips: Topping: a dollop of buttermilk and chili flakes. Swap: rice instead of bulgur (adjust cooking time accordingly). Alltags-Upgrade: toast the bulgur in butter before adding any liquid — this gives the pilaf a nutty aroma.

recipes.name: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Rice
steps: Cook rice until half done. Preheat oven to 180°C.
Cut the tops off the bell peppers and remove the seeds.
Heat oil, fry onion and garlic, add spices, then stir in half of the canned tomatoes.
Mix in the rice and season to taste — this is your filling.
Fill the peppers, place them in a baking dish, and pour the remaining tomatoes around them.
Top with cheese and bake for 30–35 Min until the peppers are tender.
recipes.tips: Topping: melted cheese and parsley. Swap: replace rice with bulgur or couscous. Alltags-Upgrade: add red beans or chickpeas to the filling for a more protein-rich and filling meal. Leftovers taste great reheated.

recipes.name: Creamy Vegetable Rice (Risotto-Style)
steps: Keep the broth hot. Melt butter, sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Briefly toast the rice in the pan.
Add the zucchini, then gradually pour in the hot broth, stirring continuously until it is absorbed.
After about 20 Min the rice will be creamy yet still have a slight bite.
Stir in the cream and cheese, then season to taste.
Let rest briefly, then serve.
recipes.tips: Topping: extra Parmesan and pepper. Swap: regular rice works fine; risotto rice will make it even creamier. Alltags-Upgrade: stir in frozen peas during the last 5 Min = color, sweetness, and more vegetables. Technik: stirring is the key to creaminess.

recipes.name: Mujadara – Rice with Lentils & Crispy Onions
steps: Pre-cook the lentils in plenty of water for about 15 Min until almost tender, then drain.
Slowly fry the onion rings in plenty of oil over medium heat until golden brown and crispy, then remove from the pan.
In the same pot, combine the rice, lentils, cumin, and cinnamon with half of the crispy onions.
Pour in about 400ml of water, season with salt, put the lid on, and simmer for 15 Min until the rice and lentils are cooked through.
Top with the remaining crispy onions.
Serve with buttermilk or yogurt.
recipes.tips: Topping: pile on the crispy onions generously and add a dollop of buttermilk. Swap: bulgur instead of rice (typical in the bazaar). Alltags-Upgrade: really take your time caramelizing the onions until deeply dark — they are the entire flavor of this dish. Leftovers taste great cold with cucumber salad.

recipes.name: Quick Tomato Soup
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Add canned tomatoes and broth, season with sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 10 Min.
Blend until smooth using an immersion blender or blender.
Stir in cream and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve with basil and bread.
recipes.tips: Topping: A swirl of cream, basil, and a few toasted sunflower seeds. Swap: Leave out the cream for a lighter version. Alltags-Upgrade: Toast bread cubes in oil until crispy (croutons) — turns this quick soup into a proper meal.

recipes.name: Quick Red Lentil Soup
steps: Heat oil, fry onion and garlic, briefly toast the spices.
Add the red lentils and peas & carrots.
Pour in the broth and simmer for 15–18 Min until the lentils fall apart.
Stir in the coconut milk and season to taste.
Blend smooth if desired.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.tips: Topping: chili flakes, a coconut milk swirl, and toasted seeds. Swap: leave out the coconut milk and use a dollop of buttermilk instead. Alltags-Upgrade: red lentils need no soaking and turn naturally creamy on their own — the ideal quick and filling meal. Keeps for 4 days.

recipes.name: Vegetable Noodle Soup
steps: Heat oil and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the frozen vegetables and briefly fry together.
Pour in the broth, add canned tomatoes if using, and bring to a boil.
Stir in the pasta and cook according to package instructions until done.
Add the peas & carrots and season to taste.
Serve garnished with parsley.
recipes.tips: Topping: Parsley and freshly ground pepper. Swap: Rice instead of pasta. Alltags-Upgrade: cook the pasta separately if you're making leftovers — otherwise it will soak up all the broth overnight. Whisk an egg into the hot soup for a silky, egg-drop-style binding. Technik: keeping the pasta separate helps maintain the right broth-to-noodle ratio when reheating.

recipes.name: Hearty Lentil Stew
steps: Heat oil and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the carrots and potatoes and briefly fry them.
Add the lentils, bay leaf, and broth.
Simmer for 30–35 Min until the lentils and potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and season to taste with salt, pepper, and a splash of vinegar.
Serve hot.
recipes.tips: Topping: a splash of vinegar and fresh parsley — the vinegar rounds out the stew beautifully. Swap: red lentils instead of brown for a creamier, quicker version. Alltags-Upgrade: tastes even better the next day; simply make a big batch and enjoy it throughout the week. Freezes well.

recipes.name: Chickpea and Spinach Stew
steps: Heat oil, fry onion, then sauté garlic and spices.
Add canned tomatoes and simmer for 5 Min.
Add chickpeas and 200ml water, simmer for 15 Min.
Stir in frozen spinach and let it cook for another 5 Min.
Season to taste and serve with bread.
recipes.tips: Topping: a dollop of buttermilk, chili flakes, and olive oil. Swap: red beans instead of chickpeas. Alltags-Upgrade: crush a few chickpeas against the side of the pan — it makes the stew creamier without any cream. Great for meal prep, keeps for 4 days.

recipes.name: Minestrone
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion, carrots, and garlic for 5 Min.
Add zucchini and briefly sauté.
Add canned tomatoes and broth, simmer for 15 Min.
Add beans and pasta, simmer for another 10 Min until the pasta is cooked.
Season to taste.
Serve with Parmesan and olive oil.
recipes.tips: Topping: Parmesan, olive oil, and pepper. Swap: any vegetables you have on hand — minestrone is a great use-it-up dish. Alltags-Upgrade: simmer a Parmesan rind along with the soup (if you have one) for incredible depth of flavor. Cook the pasta separately if you plan on having leftovers.

recipes.name: Cucumber Salad with Buttermilk
steps: Thinly slice the cucumber, lightly salt it, let it sit for 5 Min, then drain off the liquid.
Mix with buttermilk, onion, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Sprinkle with dill.
Chill briefly in the fridge.
Serve the classic way with warm jacket potatoes.
recipes.tips: Topping: fresh dill and coarsely ground pepper. Swap: cream with a splash of vinegar instead of buttermilk. Alltags-Upgrade: salt the cucumber beforehand and drain off the water — this keeps the salad nice and creamy rather than watery. Your summer classic alongside jacket potatoes.

recipes.name: Tomato & Cucumber Salad
steps: Cut the tomatoes and cucumber, slice the onion into fine rings.
Put everything in a bowl.
Whisk a dressing from oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and pour it over.
Let it sit briefly to soak.
Top with feta if you like.
recipes.tips: Topping: crumbled feta and a few olives. Swap: lemon juice instead of vinegar. Alltags-Upgrade: dip a piece of bread into the salad juices (like panzanella) — the flavorful juice is too good to throw away.

recipes.name: Tuna and Bean Salad
steps: Rinse the beans and let them drain.
Mix with the tuna, onion, and tomatoes.
Whisk together a dressing from the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Toss everything together and sprinkle with parsley.
Let the salad sit briefly to allow the flavors to meld.
recipes.tips: Topping: parsley, olive oil, and a few chili flakes. Swap: chickpeas instead of beans, or egg instead of tuna (vegetarian). Alltags-Upgrade: adding a hard-boiled egg turns the salad into a complete meal. Perfect office lunch — keeps for 2 days.

recipes.name: Power Bowl with Bulgur & Beans
steps: Pour boiling salted water over the bulgur, let it soak for 12 Min, then fluff with a fork.
Drain the beans and corn.
Dice the avocado.
Arrange the bulgur, beans, corn, and avocado in a bowl.
Whisk together lime juice, olive oil, cumin, chili, salt, and pepper to make a dressing, then pour it over.
Toss gently to combine.
recipes.tips: Topping: extra lime, chili flakes, and a dollop of buttermilk as a dressing. Swap: chickpeas instead of red beans, couscous instead of bulgur. Alltags-Upgrade: add the avocado just before serving so it doesn't brown — the rest keeps well as meal prep.

recipes.name: Rice Bowl with Egg & Peanut Dressing
ingredients: Dressing: 3 EL peanut butter, 3 EL soy sauce 🛒, 1 TL honey, water
steps: Cook the rice and let it cool.
Boil the eggs for 7 Min (soft-boiled), cool in cold water, peel, and halve.
Cut the cucumber into sticks and grate the carrot.
For the dressing, stir together the peanut butter, soy sauce, and honey with a little warm water until smooth.
Arrange the rice, vegetables, and eggs in bowls.
Top with peanut dressing and chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: peanut dressing, chili flakes, and toasted sunflower seeds. Swap: tofu or fried chickpeas instead of egg. Alltags-Upgrade: make the peanut dressing in bulk — it goes with almost any bowl, noodles, or as a veggie dip. Keeps in a jar for one week.

recipes.name: Bowl with Roasted Vegetables & Couscous
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mix the zucchini, bell pepper, onion, and chickpeas with oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper, and spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 Min until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Pour boiling salted water over the couscous, let it soak for 5 Min, then fluff with a fork.
Spoon the couscous into bowls and top with the roasted vegetables.
Top with feta and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipes.tips: Topping: feta, olive oil, and fresh parsley. Swap: bulgur instead of couscous. Alltags-Upgrade: roasting the vegetables on a baking sheet instead of frying them in a pan gives more roasted flavour and means only one sheet to wash up. Roast a large batch and enjoy as a bowl for 3 days. Technik: roasting at high heat brings out the natural sweetness of the vegetables.

recipes.name: Eggplant Parmigiana
steps: Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 15 Min, then pat dry.
For the sauce, fry the garlic in oil, add the canned tomatoes, and simmer with salt, pepper, and 1 pinch of sugar for 15 Min.
Dust the eggplant slices in a little flour and fry in oil until golden brown on both sides, then drain on kitchen paper.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
In a baking dish, layer tomato sauce, eggplant, mozzarella, and Parmesan alternately.
Finish with a layer of Parmesan and bake for 25–30 Min until golden brown. Let rest for 10 Min before cutting.
recipes.tips: Topping: fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: zucchini instead of eggplant. Alltags-Upgrade: roast the eggplant on a baking sheet instead of frying — saves oil and effort. Tastes even better the next day once it has had time to meld. Technik: salting the eggplant draws out moisture and reduces bitterness, giving you a better texture when baked.

recipes.name: Falafel with Tahini Sauce
ingredients: Tahini-Sauce: 3 EL tahini 🛒, 1 lemon 🛒, water, salt
steps: Blend chickpeas with onion, garlic, parsley, spices, and flour in a blender into a coarse mixture (not too smooth), then season with salt.
Chill the mixture for 15 Min, then shape into small balls or patties.
Fry in a pan with about 1 cm of oil until golden brown on both sides.
For the sauce, stir together tahini with lemon juice, a little water, and salt until smooth.
Drain the falafel on paper towels.
Serve with tahini sauce, couscous, and cucumber salad.
recipes.tips: Topping: Tahini sauce, tomato-cucumber salad, and chili flakes. Swap: Oven instead of pan — brush falafel with oil and bake at 200°C for 20 Min. Alltags-Upgrade: Make the mixture in bulk and freeze in portions; the tahini sauce also goes great with bowls and roasted vegetables.

recipes.name: Käsespätzle with Crispy Fried Onions
steps: Beat flour, eggs, milk, salt, and nutmeg into a thick batter until it forms bubbles, then let it rest for 10 Min.
Slowly fry the onion rings in butter until golden brown.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter in batches through a Spätzle press or a perforated board into the water.
Let the Spätzle cook until they float to the surface, then scoop them out.
Layer the Spätzle and cheese alternately in a warm bowl or dish, tossing until the cheese melts.
Top with the crispy fried onions.
recipes.tips: Topping: plenty of crispy fried onions and pepper. Swap: use ready-made Spätzle if you want to save time. Alltags-Upgrade: briefly bake the Käsespätzle in the oven at the end for a golden-brown crust. Serve with cucumber or green salad.

recipes.name: Thai-Style Vegetable Curry
ingredients: 2 TL curry powder, ½ TL chili flakes
steps: Put the rice on to cook.
Heat oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger.
Briefly toast the curry powder and chili flakes.
Add the bell pepper, zucchini, and frozen vegetables and fry for 5 Min.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the soy sauce, and simmer for 10 Min.
Season with lime juice and serve over rice.
recipes.tips: Topping: lime wedges, chili flakes, and toasted peanuts or seeds. Swap: chickpeas or tofu for extra protein. Alltags-Upgrade: a spoonful of peanut butter stirred into the sauce makes it richer and more rounded — it gets surprisingly close to that Thai flavor without any special paste. Technik:

recipes.name: Vegetable Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice Pot)
steps: Soak the rice in water for 20 Min, then drain.
Fry the eggplant, cauliflower, and carrots in oil in batches until golden brown, then remove.
Layer the fried vegetables tightly across the bottom of a pot.
Mix the rice with onion, garlic, and spices, then spread over the vegetables.
Carefully pour in just enough water to barely cover the rice, season with salt. Put the lid on and cook on low heat for 25–30 Min.
Let rest for 5 Min, then flip the pot onto a serving plate. Serve with yogurt.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted almonds and a dollop of buttermilk/yogurt. Swap: zucchini instead of eggplant, peas instead of cauliflower. Alltags-Upgrade: the flip is the showstopper moment — let it rest briefly, then turn it over with confidence. If it doesn't come out perfectly, it still tastes great; simply serve it as a layered rice dish.

recipes.name: Mushroom Risotto
steps: Keep the stock hot. Fry the mushrooms vigorously in butter, season with salt, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic in butter until translucent, then briefly toast the rice with them.
Add the hot stock ladle by ladle, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed.
After about 20 Min the rice should be creamy yet still have a little bite.
Stir in the mushrooms, Parmesan and cream, then season to taste.
Leave to rest briefly, then serve with pepper.
recipes.tips: Topping: extra Parmesan, pepper and a few reserved sautéed mushrooms. Swap: skip the cream and instead stir in a knob of cold butter at the end (mantecare). Alltags-Upgrade: constant stirring releases the starch and makes the risotto creamy — no cream substitute needed. Shape leftovers into risotto balls and fry them.

recipes.name: Veggie Halloumi Pan
ingredients: olive oil, salt, pepper, chili flakes
steps: Slice the halloumi and fry in a dry pan (no oil) until golden brown on both sides, then remove from the pan.
Add a little oil to the pan and fry the onion, bell pepper, and zucchini for 8 Min.
Season with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Return the halloumi to the pan and toss everything together briefly.
Adjust seasoning with chili flakes and serve with couscous or bread.
recipes.tips: Topping: Chili flakes and a squeeze of lemon. Swap: Feta (crumbled on cold) instead of fried halloumi. Alltags-Upgrade: Halloumi squeaks and browns best in a hot pan with no oil at all — it gives a wonderfully crispy crust. A quick, satisfying weeknight meal.

recipes.name: Quick Chickpea and Spinach Curry
ingredients: 2 TL curry powder, 1 TL cumin, ½ TL chili flakes
steps: Put the rice on to cook.
Heat oil, fry the onion and garlic, then toast the spices.
Add the chickpeas and fry briefly.
Add the coconut milk and frozen spinach, simmer for 10 Min.
Season to taste.
Serve over rice.
recipes.tips: Topping: a dollop of buttermilk, chili flakes, and toasted almonds. Swap: red beans instead of chickpeas, fresh spinach stirred in at the end. Alltags-Upgrade: mashing a few chickpeas thickens the sauce. One of the quickest satisfying veggie meals — made almost entirely from pantry staples.

recipes.name: Roasted Vegetables with Feta
ingredients: bread 🛒 or couscous as a side
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper, then spread onto a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 Min.
Scatter cubed feta on top and bake for a further 5–8 Min.
Serve with bread or couscous.
recipes.tips: Topping: Olive oil, chili flakes, and the melted feta. Swap: Halloumi instead of feta, any seasonal vegetables. Alltags-Upgrade: Roast chickpeas alongside for a complete one-pan main course. Leftovers work great cold as a bowl or spread on bread.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Stuffed Zucchini
steps: Cook the bulgur/rice until halfway done. Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Halve the zucchini lengthwise, scoop out the flesh with a spoon, and chop the flesh.
Heat oil and fry the onion, garlic, and zucchini flesh, then add the spices and half of the tomatoes.
Stir in the bulgur — this is your filling.
Fill the zucchini halves, place them in a baking dish, and spoon the remaining tomatoes around them.
Top with cheese and bake for 25 Min until the zucchini are tender.
recipes.tips: Topping: melted cheese and parsley. Swap: use bell peppers instead of zucchini. Alltags-Upgrade: stir the scooped-out zucchini flesh into the filling — zero waste and more flavour. Great to prep ahead and just bake in the evening.

recipes.name: Lentil Bolognese with Pasta
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion, carrots and garlic for 5 Min.
Briefly toast the paprika powder.
Add lentils and canned tomatoes, then pour in 400ml of water.
Simmer for 20–25 Min until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick, then season to taste.
Cook pasta al dente.
Serve with the lentil bolognese and Parmesan.
recipes.tips: Topping: Parmesan, pepper and olive oil. Swap: serve over rice or mashed potatoes instead of pasta. Alltags-Upgrade: make a double batch of the sauce and freeze it — lentil bolognese is a perfect pantry hero for quick weeknight pasta.

recipes.name: Chili sin Carne
ingredients: 1 TL cumin, 1 TL paprika, ½ TL chili flakes
steps: Heat oil, fry onion and bell pepper for 5 Min, then add garlic and spices.
Add canned tomatoes and simmer for 5 Min.
Add beans and corn, simmer on low heat for 20 Min.
Season to taste (feel free to add a little more chili).
Serve with rice or bread.
recipes.tips: Topping: grated cheese, a dollop of buttermilk, and chili flakes. Swap: red lentils instead of some of the beans for a thicker consistency. Alltags-Upgrade: a piece of dark chocolate 🛒 or a little extra cumin adds depth. Tastes even better the next day and freezes beautifully.

recipes.name: Pan-Fried Potatoes with Fried Eggs
steps: Pre-cook the potatoes in salted water for about 12 Min (or use leftovers from the day before), let them cool, then slice.
Heat oil in a pan, fry the potatoes in a single layer until golden brown, then flip — not before.
Add the onion and fry together until golden brown, season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a second pan.
Serve the pan-fried potatoes topped with the fried eggs and chives.
recipes.tips: Topping: chives, paprika, and a crispy fried egg with a runny yolk. Swap: melt cheese over the potatoes instead of using an egg. Alltags-Upgrade: day-old boiled potatoes get the crispiest — don't flip too early in the pan or they'll fall apart.

recipes.name: Jacket Potatoes with Herb Quark
steps: Cook the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 Min until tender.
Stir the quark together with the buttermilk, onion, chopped herbs, salt, pepper, and a splash of oil until smooth.
Drain the potatoes and let them steam off briefly.
Serve the jacket potatoes with the herb quark.
recipes.tips: Topping: plenty of fresh chives and coarsely ground pepper stirred into the quark. Swap: no quark — use a buttermilk cucumber salad instead. Alltags-Upgrade: a drizzle of linseed oil and toasted flaxseeds mixed into the quark = nutty and healthy, very German (Spreewald-style).

recipes.name: Rice Pudding with Cinnamon & Sugar
steps: Bring the milk to a boil with the sugar and salt.
Stir in the rice and reduce the heat.
Simmer on low heat for 25–30 Min, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and creamy.
Let it rest briefly (it will thicken further).
Serve with cinnamon sugar and fruit.
recipes.tips: Topping: Cinnamon sugar, applesauce, or banana slices with honey. Swap: use coconut milk in place of some of the milk for a more exotic flavour. Alltags-Upgrade: Stir the rice pudding at the bottom of the pot regularly to prevent sticking; leftovers served cold with fruit make a quick breakfast.

recipes.name: Potato Pancakes with Applesauce
steps: Finely grate the potatoes and onion.
Firmly squeeze out the grated mixture, removing as much liquid as possible.
Mix with eggs, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Heat oil in a pan, press small mounds flat, and fry on both sides until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with applesauce.
recipes.tips: Topping: classic applesauce, or savory with herb quark. Swap: make your own applesauce — cook apples with a little water, sugar, and cinnamon until soft. Alltags-Upgrade: really squeeze the potato mixture well — that's the whole difference between soggy and crispy.

recipes.name: Potato Gratin
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C, grease a baking dish with butter and rub it with the garlic clove.
Cut the potatoes into thin slices.
Stir together the cream and milk with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Layer the potato slices in the dish in an overlapping pattern, then pour the cream mixture over them.
Sprinkle the cheese on top and bake for 50–55 Min until the potatoes are tender and the surface is golden brown.
Let rest briefly before serving.
recipes.tips: Topping: golden-brown cheese crust and pepper. Swap: replace half the potatoes with zucchini or carrot slices. Alltags-Upgrade: slice the potatoes as thin as possible (use a mandoline) — this ensures they cook evenly and turn out creamy. Works great as a side dish or on its own with a salad.

recipes.name: Bread Dumplings with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
ingredients: Sauce: 300g button mushrooms 🛒, 1 onion, 200ml heavy cream, oil/butter
steps: Pour warm milk over the bread cubes and let soak for 15 Min.
Sauté the onion, then add to the bread along with the eggs, parsley, nutmeg, salt, and pepper; mix well.
Shape dumplings with damp hands and poach in gently simmering salted water for 15–18 Min (do not boil).
For the sauce, sauté the onion and mushrooms in butter over high heat, season with salt.
Deglaze with heavy cream, simmer briefly to reduce, and season to taste.
Serve the dumplings with the creamy mushroom sauce.
recipes.tips: Topping: parsley and pepper over the sauce. Swap: the sauce also works great with pasta or rice. Alltags-Upgrade: a perfect way to use up old bread/bread rolls; shape extra dumplings and freeze them for later. The water must only simmer — if it boils, the dumplings will fall apart.

recipes.name: Hummus
steps: Rinse the chickpeas (for extra creamy hummus, rub off the skins).
Add to a blender along with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, olive oil, and salt.
Blend until smooth, adding cold water a spoonful at a time until creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve drizzled with olive oil and a dusting of paprika.
recipes.tips: Topping: olive oil, paprika, and a few whole chickpeas. Swap: skip the tahini and use extra olive oil — slightly lighter but still delicious. Alltags-Upgrade: add an ice cube instead of water while blending for an especially airy and pale result. Keeps for 4 days — perfect as a bread spread or bowl component.

recipes.name: Baba Ganoush
steps: Preheat oven to 220°C. Pierce the eggplants several times and place on a baking tray.
Roast for 25–30 Min until the skin is black and the inside is completely soft.
Let cool slightly, scoop out the flesh, and drain off any excess liquid.
Mash or briefly blend with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and salt.
Season to taste and serve drizzled with olive oil and topped with parsley.
recipes.tips: Topping: olive oil, parsley, and paprika. Swap: roast the eggplant over an open flame or grill for a smokier flavor. Alltags-Upgrade: really roast the eggplants until deeply charred — that smoky aroma is the whole character of the dip. Serve with bread or as a side dish with falafel.

recipes.name: Tabbouleh (Bulgur Parsley Salad)
steps: Pour a small amount of boiling water over the bulgur, let it soak, then squeeze out well.
Chop the parsley very finely.
Finely dice the tomatoes and onion.
Mix everything together with the bulgur.
Whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a dressing, then stir it in.
Let the salad rest for at least 15 Min.
recipes.tips: Topping: extra lemon and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: couscous instead of bulgur. Alltags-Upgrade: traditionally, tabbouleh is very herb-heavy — don't hold back on the parsley, the bulgur is just a supporting ingredient. A fresh contrast to falafel, hummus, and roasted vegetables.

recipes.name: Imam Bayildi (Braised Stuffed Eggplants)
steps: Halve the eggplants lengthwise, score the flesh, salt them, and let sit for 15 Min, then pat dry.
Fry in olive oil on both sides, then place in a baking dish.
Sauté the onions and garlic until soft, add the cumin and canned tomatoes, and simmer with salt, pepper, and 1 pinch of sugar for 10 Min.
Spoon the tomato-onion filling into the eggplant halves.
Braise at 180°C for 25–30 Min.
Serve lukewarm or cold, garnished with parsley.
recipes.tips: Topping: plenty of parsley and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: adding chickpeas to the filling makes it more hearty. Alltags-Upgrade: tastes best lukewarm and even better cold the next day — a classic mezze dish that's great to prepare ahead. Serve with bread and hummus.

recipes.name: Vegetable Tagine with Chickpeas
ingredients: 1 TL cumin, ½ TL cinnamon, 1 TL paprika
steps: Heat oil, fry onion, briefly toast the spices.
Add carrots, bell pepper, and zucchini, fry for 5 Min.
Add canned tomatoes, chickpeas, and 200ml water.
Put the lid on and braise for 20 Min until the vegetables are tender.
Season to taste.
Serve with couscous.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted almonds and fresh parsley. Swap: sweet potato instead of carrots, whatever you have on hand. Alltags-Upgrade: the hint of cinnamon in this savory braised dish is typically North African and makes it truly special. A few raisins 🛒 highlight the sweet-savory balance.

recipes.name: Mercimek Köftesi (Lentil Balls)
steps: Cook red lentils in double the amount of water until soft and mushy.
Stir in the bulgur, remove the pot from the heat, cover and let swell for 15 Min.
Sauté the onion in oil until translucent, briefly fry the tomato paste and spices with it, then add to the lentil-bulgur mixture.
Season with lemon juice, chopped parsley, salt and pepper, and knead thoroughly.
Shape into small oval balls with wet hands.
Serve chilled on lettuce leaves.
recipes.tips: Topping: lemon, parsley, and lettuce leaves for wrapping. Swap: omit the tomato paste and use a little extra paprika instead. Alltags-Upgrade: straight from the fridge they make a great snack or mezze; the mixture keeps for 3 days and can be shaped fresh as needed. A classic on any bazaar mezze platter.

recipes.name: Peanut Noodles
ingredients: Sauce: 4 EL peanut butter, 4 EL soy sauce 🛒, 1 TL honey, 1 garlic clove 🛒, chili flakes
steps: Cook noodles according to package instructions, drain, and rinse with cold water.
For the sauce, stir together peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, pressed garlic, and chili with warm water until smooth.
Briefly sauté the bell pepper in oil (or leave it raw).
Toss the noodles with the vegetables and peanut sauce.
Serve topped with cucumber sticks and chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted peanuts/sunflower seeds, chili flakes, and raw cucumber. Swap: can be served warm or cold; soy sauce can be replaced with salt (though less authentic). Alltags-Upgrade: a squeeze of lemon juice in the sauce balances out the peanut butter. Keeps for 2 days in the fridge as a packed lunch.

recipes.name: Asian Noodle Soup (Ramen-Style)
steps: Boil eggs for 7 Min (soft-boiled/jammy), rinse in cold water, peel, and halve.
Heat oil in a pot and briefly sauté the ginger and garlic.
Pour in the broth, add the soy sauce, and bring to a boil.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook for 5 Min.
Let the noodles cook through in the broth.
Ladle into bowls and top with the eggs and chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: soft-boiled egg, chili flakes, and raw onion rings as a spring onion substitute. Swap: rice noodles or regular noodles. Alltags-Upgrade: stir 1 TL of peanut butter or tahini into the broth for a creamier, more filling soup. Ginger and garlic are the backbone of the flavor. Technik: Ingwer und Knoblauch sind das Rückgrat des Geschmacks.

recipes.name: Wok Vegetables with Almonds over Rice
steps: Cook the rice.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan, then set aside.
Heat oil in a wok or pan over high heat, briefly fry the onion, garlic, and ginger.
Stir-fry the bell pepper, zucchini, and frozen vegetables over high heat for 5–6 Min until crisp-tender.
Deglaze with soy sauce and a drizzle of honey.
Serve over rice and sprinkle with toasted almonds and chili flakes.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted almonds and chili flakes. Swap: cashews would be more classic; almonds from the pantry work just as well. Alltags-Upgrade: high heat and constant movement keep the vegetables crisp — don't overcrowd the pan or they'll steam instead of fry.

recipes.name: Potato Peanut Curry (Massaman-Style)
ingredients: 2 TL curry powder, ½ TL cinnamon, ½ TL chili flakes
steps: Heat oil, sauté onion, garlic, and ginger, then toast the curry powder, cinnamon, and chili flakes.
Add the potatoes and fry briefly.
Stir in the coconut milk, peanut butter, and soy sauce, then add about 200ml of water.
Simmer for 20–25 Min until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
Season to taste.
Serve over rice and sprinkle with toasted peanuts or almonds.
recipes.tips: Topping: toasted peanuts and a squeeze of lime. Swap: sweet potato instead of regular potato, chickpeas for extra protein. Alltags-Upgrade: the peanut butter makes the curry creamy and nutty — very close to a Massaman without any special paste. The flavors deepen the next day.

recipes.name: Mapo-Style Tofu
ingredients: 1 TL paprika, ½–1 TL chili flakes
steps: Cook the rice.
Heat oil over high heat, fry the tofu cubes on all sides, then remove from the pan.
Fry the onion, garlic, and ginger, then add the paprika and chili.
Deglaze with soy sauce and water, let simmer briefly.
Mix the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir in until the sauce thickens.
Return the tofu to the pan, toss briefly, and serve over rice.
recipes.tips: Topping: chili flakes and raw onion rings. Swap: crumbled feta or chickpeas instead of tofu. Alltags-Upgrade: pat the tofu dry thoroughly before frying and toss in cornstarch for a crispy coating that soaks up the sauce. Increase spice level to taste.

recipes.name: Vegetable Bibimbap Bowl
ingredients: Sauce: 3 EL soy sauce 🛒, 1 TL honey, 1 garlic clove 🛒, chili flakes
steps: Cook the rice.
Sauté the vegetables separately in a pan and season: zucchini, carrot, mushrooms, spinach — each with a little salt.
Fry sunny-side-up eggs (yolk still runny).
For the sauce, stir together soy sauce, honey, garlic, and chili.
Spoon rice into bowls, arrange the vegetables in a circle on top, and place an egg in the center.
Drizzle with sauce, sprinkle with sunflower seeds, and mix everything together before eating.
recipes.tips: Topping: sunny-side-up egg with a runny yolk, toasted seeds, spicy sauce. Swap: any vegetables you have on hand — bibimbap is a great colorful way to use up leftovers. Alltags-Upgrade: sautéing the vegetables separately keeps the colors and flavors distinct; the sweet-spicy sauce is what gives bibimbap its character (a substitute for gochujang).

recipes.name: Quick Soda Bread (No Rise Time)
ingredients: 400g flour (or a mix with rye flour)
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Mix together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Add the buttermilk and bring together into a dough with just a few stirs (do not knead).
Shape into a round loaf, score a cross on top, and sprinkle with seeds.
Bake for 35–45 Min until the bread sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
Let cool on a wire rack.
recipes.tips: Topping: Sunflower seeds, flaxseeds, or coarse salt before baking. Swap: Milk + 1 EL vinegar instead of buttermilk. Alltags-Upgrade: Soda bread needs no yeast and no rise time — fresh bread in one hour. Mix the dough only briefly, otherwise it will turn out tough. Technik: Keep mixing to a minimum to ensure a light, tender crumb.

recipes.name: Quick Pan Flatbread
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Add buttermilk/quark, water, and oil, then knead into a smooth dough.
Let rest for 10 Min, divide into 4 portions, and roll out thinly.
Heat a pan without oil until hot.
Cook each flatbread for 1–2 Min per side until bubbles form and brown spots appear.
Wrap warm in a cloth to keep them soft.
recipes.tips: Topping: brush with garlic butter or sprinkle with sesame seeds 🛒. Swap: yogurt instead of buttermilk. Alltags-Upgrade: perfect with hummus, baba ganoush, and falafel — fresh from the pan beats any store-bought flatbread. Toast any leftovers briefly.

recipes.name: Cheese & Herb Rolls (Quark-Oil Dough)
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C, line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Add quark, milk, and oil, then knead into a smooth dough.
Knead in the cheese and herbs.
Shape into 8 rolls and place on the tray.
Bake for 20 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: brush with milk before baking and sprinkle extra cheese or seeds on top. Swap: leave out the cheese for plain neutral rolls to serve at breakfast. Alltags-Upgrade: quark-oil dough needs no yeast and no resting time — fresh rolls in 35 Min, perfect for a spontaneous brunch.

recipes.name: Classic Mixed Wheat Bread with Yeast
steps: Dissolve the yeast and honey in lukewarm water, let stand for 5 Min.
Knead together with the flour and salt into a dough (8–10 Min) until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for 60 Min until doubled in size.
Briefly knead the dough again, shape into a loaf, place in a floured tin or on a baking tray, and let rise again for 30 Min.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and place a heatproof dish of water on the bottom (steam).
Score the top of the bread and bake for 40–45 Min until it sounds hollow when tapped.
recipes.tips: Topping: Press seeds or rolled oats onto the moist crust before baking. Swap: use only wheat flour for a lighter, softer loaf. Alltags-Upgrade: the dish of water in the oven creates steam — this gives you that crispy bakery-style crust. Let the bread cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Focaccia with Rosemary
steps: Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm water.
Mix together with flour, salt, and 3 EL olive oil to form a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise for 60 Min.
Place the dough on an oiled baking tray, spread it out with oily fingers, and press in the characteristic dimples.
Drizzle with olive oil, scatter rosemary and coarse salt on top, and let rise for another 20 Min.
Bake at 220°C for 20–25 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: rosemary, coarse salt, optionally diced tomatoes or olives 🛒. Swap: onion rings or thinly sliced potatoes as a topping. Alltags-Upgrade: using plenty of good olive oil is no place to cut corners here — it's what gives focaccia its signature moist, crispy texture. Best served warm.

recipes.name: Vegetable Quiche
ingredients: Dough: 250g flour, 125g butter (cold), 1 egg, 1 pinch of salt, 2 EL cold water
steps: Quickly knead the flour, cold butter, egg, salt, and water into a shortcrust pastry, then chill for 30 Min.
Dice the vegetables and sauté in oil for 8 Min, then let cool.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roll out the dough, place it in a greased tin, press up the edges, and prick all over with a fork.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Spread the vegetables over the dough and pour the egg mixture on top.
Bake for 35–40 Min until the filling is set and golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: extra cheese and pepper; fresh herbs after baking. Swap: frozen spinach or mushrooms as a filling. Alltags-Upgrade: tastes great warm and cold — ideal for preparing ahead and as lunch the next day. Serve with a green salad for a complete meal.

recipes.name: Classic Cheesecake
ingredients: Crust: 200g flour, 80g sugar, 100g butter, 1 egg, 1 TL baking powder
steps: Knead flour, sugar, butter, egg, and baking powder into a shortcrust pastry, then chill for 20 Min.
Press the dough into a greased springform pan, pulling the edges up the sides.
Mix quark, sugar, eggs, pudding powder, melted butter, milk, and salt until smooth.
Pour the filling over the crust and spread evenly.
Bake at 170°C for about 60 Min until the surface is golden and just set.
Let cool in the switched-off oven with the door slightly ajar (this prevents cracking).
recipes.tips: Topping: plain, dusted with powdered sugar 🛒, or topped with a few frozen berries 🛒. Swap: add lemon zest or juice to the filling for a fresh twist. Alltags-Upgrade: cooling the cheesecake slowly in the oven keeps it from sinking and cracking — patience is the whole trick here.

recipes.name: Marble Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C, grease and flour a bundt or loaf pan.
Beat butter with sugar and salt until creamy, then mix in eggs one at a time.
Mix flour with baking powder, then fold in alternately with the milk.
Pour two thirds of the batter into the pan.
Stir cocoa and 1 EL milk into the remaining batter, spoon the dark batter on top, then draw a fork through both batters in a spiral motion.
Bake for 50–55 Min (skewer test), leave to cool, then turn out.
recipes.tips: Topping: Powdered sugar 🛒 or a thin chocolate glaze 🛒. Swap: replace some of the milk with buttermilk for a moister result. Alltags-Upgrade: draw the fork through the batter only once and loosely — too much swirling will blur the marble pattern. Stays moist for 4 days.

recipes.name: Moist Lemon Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C, grease and flour a loaf pan.
Beat butter with sugar until creamy, then mix in eggs one at a time.
Add lemon zest and juice.
Mix flour with baking powder and salt, then stir into the batter.
Pour into the pan and bake for 40–45 Min (skewer test).
While still warm, spread with lemon powdered sugar glaze.
recipes.tips: Topping: lemon glaze and a little grated lemon zest. Swap: orange instead of lemon. Alltags-Upgrade: poke the still-warm cake all over with a skewer and soak with lemon syrup (juice + sugar) — makes it extra moist and intensely flavored.

recipes.name: Carrot Cake
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease the tin.
Beat eggs with sugar until fluffy, then stir in the oil.
Mix together flour, baking powder, almonds, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt, then stir into the batter.
Fold in the grated carrots.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40–45 Min (check with a skewer), then leave to cool.
Beat cream cheese with powdered sugar until smooth and spread over the cooled cake.
recipes.tips: Topping: Cream cheese frosting and chopped almonds/walnuts 🛒. Swap: skip the frosting and dust with powdered sugar instead. Alltags-Upgrade: Grate the carrots really finely so they melt into the batter; the almonds keep it wonderfully moist. It tastes even better on the second day. Technik: Make sure the cake is fully cooled before spreading the frosting so it doesn't slide off.

recipes.name: Chocolate Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C and line a square baking pan with parchment paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter over a double boiler or carefully in a saucepan, then let cool slightly.
Beat eggs with sugar and salt until fluffy, then stir in the chocolate mixture.
Fold in the flour and cocoa powder — do not overmix — then add the almonds.
Pour into the pan and bake for 25–30 Min — the center should still be slightly moist.
Let cool completely, then cut into squares.
recipes.tips: Topping: Powdered sugar 🛒 or a scoop of vanilla ice cream 🛒 with a warm brownie. Swap: Replace almonds with walnuts 🛒 or chocolate chips. Alltags-Upgrade: don't bake them all the way through — brownies should stay fudgy in the middle; it's better to take them out 2 Min too early than too late.

recipes.name: Banana Bread
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C and grease a loaf pan.
Mash the bananas with a fork.
Stir in the sugar, melted butter, and eggs.
Mix together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt, then stir into the banana mixture.
Fold in the almonds/chocolate chips, then pour the batter into the pan.
Bake for 50–55 Min (test with a skewer), then let cool.
recipes.tips: Topping: place a few banana slices on top of the batter before baking, or spread peanut butter on each slice. Swap: replace half the flour with oats for more texture. Alltags-Upgrade: the riper (browner) the bananas, the sweeter and more moist the bread — a perfect way to use up overripe bananas.

recipes.name: Plum Crumble Cake
ingredients: Dough: 250g flour, 100g sugar, 125g butter, 1 egg, 1 TL baking powder
Crumble: 200g flour, 150g butter, 100g sugar, 1 TL cinnamon
steps: Knead flour, sugar, butter, egg, and baking powder into a shortcrust pastry, then chill briefly.
Work flour, sugar, cinnamon, and cold butter together with your fingers to form crumbles.
Preheat oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Press the dough onto the tray, pulling the edges up slightly.
Arrange the plum halves closely on top.
Scatter the crumble over the top and bake for 35–40 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: Powdered sugar 🛒 or a dollop of cream. Swap: Frozen berries or apricots instead of plums (depending on the season). Alltags-Upgrade: sprinkle a little semolina or ground almonds onto the dough before adding the plums — it absorbs the juice and keeps the base crispy.

recipes.name: Berry Sheet Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C, line baking sheet with parchment paper.
Beat butter and sugar until creamy, then mix in eggs one at a time.
Combine flour with baking powder and salt, then fold in alternately with the milk.
Spread the batter evenly over the baking sheet.
Distribute berries evenly on top (do not thaw frozen berries — toss them lightly in flour first).
Bake for 35–40 Min, let cool, then dust with powdered sugar.
recipes.tips: Topping: Powdered sugar or whipped cream; add a few fresh berries on top. Swap: any berry mix or cherries. Alltags-Upgrade: Toss frozen berries in a little flour before placing them on the batter — this keeps them from sinking and prevents them from turning the cake blue.

recipes.name: Spice Cake
ingredients: ½ TL ground cloves 🛒, 1 TL ground ginger 🛒
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C and grease a loaf pan.
Beat butter with sugar and honey until creamy, then stir in eggs one at a time.
Mix flour with baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ginger, and salt.
Fold into the butter mixture alternately with the milk.
Pour into the pan and bake for 45–50 Min (check with a skewer).
Leave to cool, then glaze with icing sugar if desired.
recipes.tips: Topping: a thin drizzle of icing 🛒 or a dusting of powdered sugar, plus a few chopped almonds. Swap: if you don't have all the spices on hand, just use cinnamon and nutmeg from your pantry. Alltags-Upgrade: tastes best on day 2–3 once it's had time to rest — the spices mellow and round out beautifully. Perfect for the cold season with a cup of tea.

recipes.name: Vanilla Pudding with Banana
steps: Whisk the pudding powder with sugar and approx. 6 EL of the cold milk until smooth.
Bring the remaining milk to a boil.
Stir in the mixed powder and let it boil vigorously for 1 Min, stirring constantly.
Distribute the banana slices into glasses or bowls.
Pour the pudding over the top.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and almonds, then refrigerate.
recipes.tips: Topping: bananas, cinnamon, and toasted almonds; a dollop of peanut butter works surprisingly well. Swap: chocolate pudding instead of vanilla; any fruit instead of banana. Alltags-Upgrade: fold in a layer of crumbled cookies 🛒 or oats for a quick layered dessert. Pressing a sheet of plastic wrap directly onto the pudding prevents a skin from forming.

recipes.name: Chocolate Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix together the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, and salt.
Whisk together the eggs, oil, and milk, then add to the dry ingredients and stir briefly.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Fill the cases with batter (to 2/3 full).
Bake for 18–20 Min (toothpick test).
recipes.tips: Topping: place a few chocolate chips on top of the batter before baking. Swap: leave out the cocoa and bake vanilla muffins instead. Alltags-Upgrade: only stir the batter briefly — small lumps are fine; overmixing makes muffins tough and flat. Technik: keeping the mixing to a minimum prevents too much gluten from developing, which keeps the muffins light and fluffy.

recipes.name: Banana Oat Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and prepare a muffin tin.
Mash the bananas and mix with the eggs, oil, and sugar/honey.
Combine the flour, rolled oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt, then stir into the wet mixture.
Spoon the batter into the muffin cases.
Bake for 18–20 Min (check with a skewer).
Allow to cool completely.
recipes.tips: Topping: sprinkle a few rolled oats or banana slices on top before baking. Swap: fold in 50g of almonds or chocolate chips. Alltags-Upgrade: using honey instead of sugar and very ripe bananas means these muffins need hardly any added sugar — a great breakfast to go. They freeze well too.

recipes.name: Apple Cinnamon Muffins
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C and prepare a muffin tin.
Dice the apples into small pieces.
Mix together the eggs, oil, milk, and sugar.
Combine flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt, stir into the wet mixture, then fold in the apple pieces.
Fill the muffin cases with the batter.
Bake for 20 Min (check with a skewer).
recipes.tips: Topping: Sprinkle a cinnamon-sugar mixture over the batter before baking for a crispy top. Swap: Use pear instead of apple. Alltags-Upgrade: A handful of chopped almonds or crumble topping sprinkled on top turns these muffins into a little treat. Keep the apple pieces small so they don't sink to the bottom.

recipes.name: Blueberry Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and prepare a muffin tin.
Mix together the eggs, melted butter, milk, and sugar.
Combine the flour, baking powder, salt, and lemon zest, then briefly stir into the wet mixture.
Lightly coat the blueberries in flour and gently fold them in.
Spoon the batter into the muffin cases.
Bake for 20–22 Min (check with a skewer).
recipes.tips: Topping: place a few berries and a little sugar on top for a crispy domed crust. Swap: raspberries or mixed frozen berries. Alltags-Upgrade: toss the berries in flour so they don't sink to the bottom; don't thaw frozen berries beforehand or the batter will turn purple.

recipes.name: Savory Cheese Muffins
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C and prepare a muffin tin.
Grate the zucchini and squeeze out well.
Whisk together the eggs, oil, and milk.
Mix flour, baking powder, paprika, salt, and pepper, then stir into the wet ingredients.
Fold in the cheese and zucchini.
Fill the muffin cases and bake for 20 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: add extra cheese on top of the batter before baking. Swap: corn 🛒, diced bell pepper, or herbs instead of zucchini. Alltags-Upgrade: savory muffins are the perfect lunchbox and brunch treat and taste best slightly warm. Squeeze the zucchini out well, otherwise the muffins will turn out soggy. Technik: squeeze the zucchini out well, otherwise the muffins will turn out soggy.

recipes.name: Lemon-Almond Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and prepare a muffin tin.
Mix together the eggs, melted butter, milk, sugar, lemon juice, and lemon zest.
Combine the flour, almonds, baking powder, and salt, then briefly fold into the wet mixture.
Spoon the batter into the muffin cases.
Bake for 20 Min (check with a skewer).
Drizzle with a little lemon icing sugar while still warm.
recipes.tips: Topping: Lemon glaze 🛒 and flaked almonds. Swap: Use orange instead of lemon. Alltags-Upgrade: the ground almonds keep the muffins moist for a long time; scattering a few almond flakes on top adds a satisfying crunch and looks elegant.

recipes.name: Starting & Maintaining a Sourdough Starter
ingredients: Rye or wheat flour (whole grain gets going faster)
steps: Day 1: Stir 50g flour and 50g lukewarm water together in the jar, cover loosely, and leave at room temperature.
Days 2–3: Stir daily; the first bubbles should start to appear.
From Day 3: 'feed' daily — remove half (keep the discard!) and refresh with 50g flour and 50g water each.
Days 5–7: When the starter doubles within 4–6 hrs after feeding and smells pleasantly sour and fruity, it's ready to bake with.
Storage: keep the active starter in the fridge and feed it 1×/week.
Before baking, refresh 1–2× at room temperature until it's actively bubbling.
recipes.tips: Topping/Verwendung: use an active starter for bread, pizza, and focaccia; use the removed discard for pancakes or crackers — don't throw anything away. Swap: whole rye flour gets started more reliably than white flour. Alltags-Upgrade: if there's a good bakery nearby, a spoonful of their mature starter can cut the whole project down to 1–2 days. Mark the jar with a rubber band to track the rise.

recipes.name: Sourdough Bread (Loaf)
ingredients: a little flour for working the dough
steps: Roughly combine the starter, flour, and water, then let rest for 30–60 Min (autolyse).
Work in the salt. Over 2–3 Std, stretch and fold the dough in the bowl every 30 Min.
Cover the dough and let it rise at room temperature for 4–6 Std until noticeably increased in size.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and place it in a floured proofing basket or a bowl lined with a cloth.
Let it proof overnight in the refrigerator for 8–14 Std.
Preheat the oven with a pot (Dutch Oven) to 240°C. Score the dough, bake in the hot pot with the lid on for 20 Min, then remove the lid and bake for a further 20–25 Min until golden brown.
Let the loaf cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.
recipes.tips: Topping: Press seeds or rolled oats onto the moist crust; top with cheese for a savory version. Swap: without a Dutch Oven, place a dish of water in the oven to create steam. Alltags-Upgrade: the cold overnight proof develops the characteristic tangy flavor and fits perfectly into daily life — set it up in the evening, bake in the morning. Be patient when cooling, otherwise the crumb will be gummy.

recipes.name: Sourdough Pizza
ingredients: Belag: tomato sauce, cheese, vegetables of your choice
steps: Knead the starter, flour, water, salt, and oil into a smooth dough.
Cover and let rise at room temperature for 4–6 hours until noticeably puffed (or overnight in the fridge).
Divide into 2 balls and let rest for 30 Min.
Preheat the oven as hot as possible (250°C+), heating a baking sheet or stone along with it.
Stretch the dough thin with your hands and add your toppings.
Bake for 8–12 Min until the crust has puffed up and is nicely browned.
recipes.tips: Topping: finish with fresh basil 🛒 and a drizzle of olive oil. Swap: also works with regular yeast dough if you don't have an active starter. Alltags-Upgrade: really crank the oven up to full heat and preheat the baking sheet — intense bottom heat is what makes the crust crispy. Leftover dough keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days and develops even more flavor.

recipes.name: Sourdough Discard Pancakes
steps: Mix the discard with the egg and milk.
Stir in the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt to form a thick batter.
Heat butter in a pan.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter into the pan and cook over medium heat, flipping when bubbles appear on the surface.
Cook until golden brown.
Serve with honey, banana, or berries.
recipes.tips: Topping: banana, honey, or berries; also great savory with cheese. Swap: leaving out the baking powder makes them flatter and tangier (more of a crêpe style). Alltags-Upgrade: a perfect way to use up your sourdough starter discard — no waste. The sourdough gives a pleasantly tangy flavor.

recipes.name: Sourdough Discard Crackers
steps: Knead the discard together with flour, olive oil, salt, seeds, and spices into a smooth dough.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Roll the dough out very thinly between two sheets of baking paper.
Peel off the top sheet of baking paper, sprinkle the dough with coarse salt, and score into diamonds or rectangles.
Bake for 20–25 Min until golden brown and crispy.
Let cool on the baking sheet, then break into pieces.
recipes.tips: Topping: coarse salt, sesame 🛒 or herbs before baking. Swap: paprika and chili flakes for spicy crackers. Alltags-Upgrade: roll out as thinly as possible — the thinner, the crispier. Goes perfectly with hummus and baba ganoush and makes great use of your discard.

recipes.name: Sourdough Focaccia
steps: Mix starter, flour, water, and salt into a soft, sticky dough.
Over 2–3 Std, stretch and fold once every 45 Min.
Cover and let rise for several hours (or overnight in the fridge) until airy.
Turn the dough onto a well-oiled baking sheet, press it out with oily fingers, and dimple the surface all over.
Drizzle with olive oil, scatter over rosemary and coarse salt, then let rest for 30–45 Min.
Bake at 220°C for 20–25 Min until golden brown.
recipes.tips: Topping: Rosemary, coarse salt, chopped tomatoes or olives 🛒. Swap: A discard-heavy version with a little extra yeast if your starter is weak. Alltags-Upgrade: the long, cold rise makes the focaccia especially airy and flavourful — mix it in the evening and bake it the next day. A generous amount of olive oil gives you that classic crispy-yet-moist crust. Technik: keep your hands well oiled when dimpling — this prevents sticking and helps the dough spread evenly.

recipes.name: Quick Tomato Sauce (Base)
steps: Heat olive oil, sauté onion until translucent, briefly fry garlic with it.
Add canned tomatoes, season with salt, pepper, and 1 pinch of sugar.
Simmer on low heat for 15–20 Min, stirring occasionally.
Blend smooth if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
recipes.tips: Topping: base for pasta, pizza, casseroles, and shakshuka. Swap: stir in cream to make a tomato cream sauce, or add vegetables for a complete pasta sauce. Alltags-Upgrade: make a double batch and freeze in portions — the fastest route to a weeknight meal. A pinch of sugar takes the edge off the acidity of canned tomatoes.

recipes.name: Cheese Cream Sauce (Béchamel Base)
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1–2 Min over medium heat, stirring (do not brown).
Gradually pour in the milk, stirring constantly, until a smooth sauce forms.
Simmer for 5 Min until thickened.
Stir in the cheese until melted, then season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
recipes.tips: Topping: use for lasagne, casseroles, over vegetables (e.g. cauliflower), or as a pasta sauce. Swap: omit the cheese for a plain béchamel. Alltags-Upgrade: add the milk in small amounts and stir well — guaranteed lump-free. A little mustard 🛒 or an egg yolk makes it even more rounded in flavor. Technik: always keep stirring when adding the milk to prevent lumps.

recipes.name: Pesto (with Almonds)
steps: Toast the almonds briefly in a dry pan, then let them cool.
Add the basil, almonds, Parmesan, and garlic to the blender.
Add the olive oil and blend into a rough paste.
Season to taste with salt, pepper, and a little lemon.
Transfer to a jar and cover with a thin layer of oil.
recipes.tips: Topping: for pasta, on bread, in soups, or over roasted vegetables. Swap: sunflower seeds instead of almonds, parsley instead of basil. Alltags-Upgrade: covered with a thin layer of oil, pesto keeps in the fridge for 1–2 weeks; freeze in ice cube trays for individual portions.

recipes.name: Tahini Dressing
steps: Mix the tahini with lemon juice and garlic — the mixture will initially become thick and lumpy.
Stir in cold water one spoonful at a time until the dressing suddenly turns creamy and pourable.
Season with salt and a little cumin to taste.
Add more water to reach your desired consistency.
recipes.tips: Topping: over falafel, bowls, roasted vegetables, salads, or as a dip. Swap: mixed with yogurt 🛒 it becomes milder and more dip-like. Alltags-Upgrade: don't be alarmed if the mixture clumps at first — that's normal; adding water will make it turn silky almost instantly. Keeps in the fridge for one week.

recipes.name: Vinaigrette (Salad Base)
steps: Mix the vinegar, mustard, honey, salt, and pepper together in a jar.
Slowly stir in the olive oil, or seal the jar and shake vigorously until emulsified.
Add finely chopped onion if desired.
Taste and adjust — add more acid or oil to your liking.
recipes.tips: Topping: use on any green salad, tomato-cucumber salad, or drizzled over roasted vegetables. Swap: lemon juice instead of vinegar, maple syrup instead of honey. Alltags-Upgrade: the mustard is the emulsifier — it binds the oil and acid into a creamy vinaigrette that won't separate. It keeps for one week in a jar; shake before use.

recipes.name: Universal Pizza Dough (Yeast Dough)
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in lukewarm water, let stand for 5 Min.
Knead together with flour, salt, and olive oil into a smooth, elastic dough (8–10 Min).
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 45–60 Min until doubled in size.
Briefly knead the dough again, then divide into portions.
Roll or stretch out thinly and add toppings.
Bake at the highest oven temperature (250°C+) for 10–12 Min.
recipes.tips: Usage: Base for pizza, flatbread, focaccia, or savory stuffed dough pockets. Swap: half the flour with whole wheat flour for more flavor. Alltags-Upgrade: Prepare the dough the day before and let it rise overnight in the fridge — it develops more flavor and is ready to bake when you get home. Make sure to fully preheat the oven.
